items.title: 56711_Buster Smith oral history interview
items.q: She said, "Buster, do you mean to tell me I've been paying this brother of yours all this much money all this long time, and that man can't read no music?"

ctx.x: playing the music right. He's can't play it." He said, "Well, I can't see that. My eyes bad. I can't see that." She said, "I've got to work. Somebody got to play my act. You got to play." So the boss lady was sitting down there on the chair right there on the bandstand, looking. She said, "Buster, do you mean to tell me I've been paying this brother of yours all this much money all this long time, and that man can't read no music?" I said, "Oh yeah, he can read it, Miss Holt, but he's just a little slow. I'll…

So I kind of talked to the girl, and I take the music and carried it around the corner there to my girlfriend's house, and sat down all of the evenin', the rest of the evenin', and wrote it out and played it on my alto. And he followed me on the alto. That's the only thing he did. And I just played all the technical parts in there.
